subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI scroll-jump fix be owned as default viewport anchoring, an upstream/pi-tui renderer repair, or a new user-facing TUI scroll mode?
rationale: The current source path is credible, but the permanent fix affects terminal UX policy and may cross the renderer dependency boundary or add a new user-facing mode.

options.title: Repair anchoring first
options.body: Prefer a live-proven default fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping the viewport and follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add an explicit TUI scroll mode
options.body: Expose a user-facing follow/preserve mode, accepting the extra CLI/docs/tests and upgrade-proof burden.

options.title: Wait for upstream renderer proof
options.body: Keep the tracker open until the pi-tui scrollback-clearing path is fixed upstream or a current-main PTY capture proves a narrower OpenClaw-side repair.

recommendation.title: Repair anchoring first
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven default fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping the viewport and follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on the TUI ChatLog/session state surface that would need to encode the chosen behavior.
